result.summary: The pedestrian environment features continuous sidewalks and a signalized intersection with marked crosswalks. However, the lack of a physical buffer between the walkway and the roadway, combined with blank building frontages, reduces the overall sense of safety and comfort for walkers.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the travel lane without any physical separation like trees or parked cars.

hazards.name: Blank Frontage
hazards.description: The building on the left has a long stretch of blank wall and closed shutters, which reduces natural surveillance.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the intersection to shorten the crossing distance and increase pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Plant street trees to provide a vertical buffer between pedestrians and vehicles and improve the streetscape.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a wide, multi-lane roadway with a continuous sidewalk that lacks a protective buffer from traffic. The presence of large curb cuts and the absence of marked crossings or traffic calming measures prioritize vehicle throughput over pedestrian safety. Mature street trees provide some shade but do not offer physical protection from the adjacent high-speed travel lanes.

hazards.name: Wide Roadway
hazards.description: The four-lane configuration encourages high vehicle speeds and creates a long, unprotected crossing distance.

hazards.name: Large Curb Cut
hazards.description: A wide vehicle access point in front of the red building creates a large conflict zone where cars cross the sidewalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Sidewalk in front of red building

hazards.name: Lack of Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the roadway, exposing pedestrians to traffic noise and potential vehicle incursions.

interventions.title: Road Diet
interventions.description: Reducing the number of travel lanes to slow traffic and shorten crossing distances.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Providing a safe waiting area in the center of the wide roadway for midblock crossings.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Narrowing the roadway at key points to improve visibility and reduce crossing distance.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of wide sidewalks but lacks any marked crossings or traffic calming measures along a wide, multi-lane roadway. Significant curb cuts for commercial vehicle access and a lack of physical buffers between the walkway and traffic increase the risk of conflict.

hazards.name: Wide Curb Cut
hazards.description: A large driveway for the tire shop creates a wide conflict zone where vehicles cross the sidewalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image at the tire shop

hazards.name: Lack of Crossing Infrastructure
hazards.description: The wide roadway has no marked crosswalks or refuge islands visible, making crossing difficult and dangerous.

interventions.title: Mid-block Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install a high-visibility marked crosswalk with signage to provide a legal and safer crossing point.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Narrow the roadway at potential crossing points to reduce pedestrian exposure and slow vehicle speeds.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffers
interventions.description: Add a planting strip or street trees to create a physical and psychological barrier between the sidewalk and moving traffic.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a wide sidewalk that is in poor physical condition with significant cracking and uneven surfaces. The streetscape is dominated by shuttered commercial storefronts and lacks any buffer or greenery between the walkway and the roadway.

hazards.name: Uneven Pavement
hazards.description: The sidewalk is composed of cracked and mismatched concrete slabs, creating tripping hazards for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the entire visible sidewalk area.

hazards.name: Lack of Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation or buffer zone between the pedestrian walkway and the adjacent roadway.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Repair
interventions.description: Repave the sidewalk to create a smooth, level, and continuous surface for all users.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Furniture Zone
interventions.description: Install street trees or a furniture zone to provide a buffer from traffic and improve the pedestrian experience.
